# Modules that boot a real system in tests WITHOUT using systemscenario.
# Generated by: bash scripts/check-systemscenario-adoption.sh --update
# (re-run it to re-measure; this file is hand-reviewed, so reasons survive)
#
# Every row is a deliberate choice, so every row needs a REASON:
#   <module><TAB><why the lower-level boot is the right tool here>
# A module that adopts the harness disappears from this list; the gate fails on
# an unlisted offender, on a stale row, and on an empty reason.
#
# module	reason
benchkit	benchmark fixtures boot a system to measure latency; the assertions are metric-based, not behavioral
cmd/doc-check	compiles documentation fences; the boot proves the snippet runs, and the fence text is the assertion
metaengine	the auto-projection spike proves one wiring path; metaengine's own suites are engine-level conformance
system	unit-level tests for the composition root itself; the system-level BDD tier lives in systemscenario/systemtest
system/integration	real-engine integration legs (duckdb/postgres) assert engine wiring the scenario DSL does not model
systemcatalog	derivation tests boot an ephemeral system to read registration records; no dispatch and no fold
systemtest	crash/shutdown/durability paths; the DSL models behavior, these model process death and restart
